subtopics.title: Three Bills and Their Scope
subtopics.summary: The 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025 is one of three Bills tabled by the Home Minister, and together the Bills propose the removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers under certain conditions. A Joint Parliamentary Committee is examining the Bill and is expected to finalise and adopt its report. The other two Bills are the Government of Union Territories (Amendment) Bill, 2025 and the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2025.
facts: Introduced in 2025 as the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill
Three Bills tabled by the Home Minister
Bill 1: Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025
Bill 2: Government of Union Territories (Amendment) Bill, 2025
Bill 3: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2025
The Bills propose removal of Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers under certain conditions
Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) is examining the 130th Amendment Bill
The JPC is expected to finalise and adopt its report

subtopics.title: Governance Implications and Concerns
subtopics.summary: The Bill is presented as strengthening ethical governance by stopping leaders from holding power while facing serious criminal charges. It is also described as bridging a gap in the Representation of the People Act, which disqualifies legislators only after conviction. The booklet records several concerns, including misuse of arrests against opposition-led states, a threat to federalism and the presumption of innocence.
facts: The Bill upholds constitutional morality and ethical governance
It stops leaders from retaining power while facing serious criminal charges
It removes the 'governance from jail' anomaly
It protects public trust by acting against criminalisation of politics
It bridges a legal gap: the RPA disqualifies only post-conviction, while the Bill addresses interim arrests
Concern: the Centre could destabilise opposition-led states through targeted arrests
Concern: the Bill reduces the autonomy of elected state leaders, threatening federalism
Concern: removal based solely on detention contravenes 'innocent until proven guilty'
Concern: ED and CBI could be exploited to arrest leaders on weak charges

subtopics.title: Passage of a Constitution Amendment Bill
subtopics.summary: A Constitution amendment Bill can be introduced in either House, but it must be passed by both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Once passed, it is presented to the President, who is bound to give consent, and the Bill then becomes an Act. The booklet also links the process to the Anti-Defection Law and related constitutional articles.
facts: The Bill can be introduced either in Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
The Bill must be passed by both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Lok Sabha strength is 545 members
In a tie, the Presiding Officer of a house can cast his or her vote
The passed Bill is presented to the President
The President is bound to give consent
After assent the Bill becomes an Act
Related provisions: Articles 102 and 191, the Anti-Defection Law and the Lily Thomas case
